structure: Independent people follow Z=G0, X=0.6Z+0.8G1, and Y=0.6Z+0.8(0.25G1+sqrt(1-0.25^2)G2), with independent standard normal G0,G1,G2. The residual correlation is an explicitly chosen scenario.

parameter_provenance.basis: Exact marginal Pearson correlations in the common population.
Each population OLS slope is correlation times outcome SD divided by Z SD; all SDs equal one.
Chosen completion of the unreported X-Y relationship; not implied by adjustment for Z.
Convenient distributional completion satisfying the supplied moments.
Conditional on the assumed residual correlation: 0.6*0.6+0.64*0.25=0.52.

requested_estimands.name: partial_xy_given_z
requested_estimands.basis: Pearson correlation of separate intercept-and-Z OLS residuals equals (rXY-0.36)/0.64. The records do not determine rXY; this model chooses residual correlation 0.25.

requested_estimands.name: marginal_xy
requested_estimands.basis: The chosen residual covariance is 0.64*0.25=0.16, so Cov(X,Y)=0.36+0.16=0.52. Both variables have unit variance.

requested_estimands.name: slope_x_on_z
requested_estimands.basis: For population OLS with an intercept, the slope is Cov(X,Z)/Var(Z)=0.6/1, using B and C only.

limitations: The supplied records permit marginal X-Y correlations throughout [-0.28,1], corresponding to residual correlations throughout [-1,1]; neither requested correlation is point identified.
Gaussian shape and the selected residual dependence are modeling assumptions, not reported evidence. Gaussianity is not needed to identify the X-on-Z slope.
Standardization holds at the population level. Random finite samples are not recentered, rescaled, selected, or otherwise forced to match population moments.
This artificial mathematical model provides no clinical validation or causal interpretation.
checks_actually_performed: Analytically verified zero population means, unit variances, and correlations Corr(X,Z)=Corr(Y,Z)=0.6.

Analytically checked positive definiteness: the scenario correlation matrix has leading principal minors 1, 0.7296, and 0.384.
Analytically obtained the admissible marginal-correlation interval from (rXY-0.36)^2<=0.64^2.
